introduction.goalContent: Architect and deploy web applications that merge a Back-End with Front-End interfaces, automating corporate workflows and enabling secure, scalable, and user-oriented digital platforms.
introduction.journeyContent: I started my career developing and optimizing web systems in the manufacturing sector, where I built ASP.NET Core platforms to automate logistical and financial calculations. Currently, I lead web development and software architecture in the ERP consulting sector, programming commercial portals, structuring PostgreSQL databases, and deploying internal applications to guarantee the technical stability of business operations.
introduction.locationSubtitle: Base of operations and geographic availability
introduction.aboutContent:
I am a Web Developer focused on building software architectures and solutions. I transform business logic into fast and intuitive web applications. My focus is on designing the Back-End for efficient data processing and structuring the Front-End to improve the user experience, making it smooth and friction-free.

My work provides companies with high-performance platforms. By integrating web solutions and APIs, I make it easier for operational teams to interact with real-time information through accessible interfaces. This not only optimizes server performance and reduces load times, but also ensures that each developed module brings direct value to the business operation.

img5.title: Budget Control Web Platform
img5.desc: I develop from scratch a corporate web application for the finance area with the goal of mitigating operational risks through expense monitoring. I structure the Back-End architecture in ASP.NET Core 8.0 using C# to automate the extraction and cross-referencing of data from the Oracle system, backing up the information in SQL Server databases. I connect this logic with a smooth user interface and integrate Microsoft Identity to manage secure access control, allowing the finance department to generate calculated reports instantly through the browser.

img3.title: Labels
img3.desc: Desktop application developed for the Warehouse area to improve supplier traceability associated with each product. It allows querying, based on the order number, the Supplier Part Number and the Daikin Part Number, connecting to an API that executes the query in Oracle. The data is sent directly to the printer to generate the label, which includes a barcode for easy scanning. Label generation was done with NuGet iText 5.5.13.5. The system incorporates a JSON configuration file that allows users to adjust the label size without requiring code changes. Reduced process times by over 50%.

img4.title: MasterLabels Analytical System
img4.desc: I develop an analytical web platform (using ASP.NET and MySQL) focused on diagnosing and resolving technical desynchronization in printing logistics labels. I program the system to perform the ingestion of large volumes of granular data, building an interactive Front-End interface that renders dashboards and dynamic tables for user evaluation. This software solution isolated failure patterns in real-time, allowing the implementation of a latency adjustment on the server that plummeted the incidence rate from 8,000 to less than 100 monthly.

img2.title: Overtime Request Portal
img2.desc: I manage and optimize an internal web application in C# and ASP.NET designed to calculate the costs generated by overtime logistics services. I program the Front-End with Bootstrap to ensure responsive navigation for supervisors by plant and structure the server-side logic to automate exact financial calculations. I reinforce the portal architecture by integrating SSO authentication protocols, ensuring that system access from any device is aligned with corporate cybersecurity policies.

img1.title: Corporate E-commerce Web Development

I optimize the Front-End architecture to ensure minimal load times and connect web navigation directly with internal CRM and Sales modules in the Back-End, unifying the customer experience with the company's operations.
